claim: Technical explanation in a list discussion, including a cited release-note description; not a controlled reproduction report. A participant explains that hold/resume and supplementary call operations could leave media inactive when a third-party endpoint returned an inactive SDP answer where the older call flow expected send/receive media. The thread also discusses the changed behavior in CUCM 8.5. Outcome noted in the thread: Historical version-dependent interoperability behavior is described; no specific customer call is confirmed as repaired in this thread.
versionOrJurisdiction: Historical Cisco VoIP mailing-list post dated 2011-04-15; product context: CUCM before 8.5 is explicitly discussed; no complete deployed version matrix is stated.
uncertainty: Applies to the described historical offer/answer behavior and counterpart implementations; not a general claim about current SIP endpoints. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.

claim: Customer-style incident report plus troubleshooting suggestions and a separate claimed fix. A reported phone-to-phone call transferred blindly through a CUBE/SIP trunk to an external mobile had one-way audio. Replies discuss SDP direction attributes and a SIP-profile option limited to early-offer trunks; one participant says header manipulation fixed a separate instance. Outcome noted in the thread: The archive does not confirm that the original reporter's call was fixed. A reply reports one other instance repaired with SBC header manipulation.
versionOrJurisdiction: Historical Cisco VoIP mailing-list post dated 2014-04-30; product context: CUCM, CUBE and a Lync interoperation example are mentioned; exact versions are not stated in the initial report.
uncertainty: SDP address appearance alone did not establish working RTP in the report. The proposed profile setting is conditional on early offer and should not become a blanket remedy. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.

claim: Reproducible report across two systems and a reply attributing it to a particular firmware bug. A 9951 with expansion module could place calls using a busy-lamp-field speed dial, but using that key during a transfer created another call instead of completing transfer. Manual destination dialing worked. Outcome noted in the thread: Reply recommends an engineering special; archive does not include the reporter's confirmation of the fix.
versionOrJurisdiction: Historical Cisco VoIP mailing-list post dated 2013-04-02; product context: Thread title identifies CUCM 9.1; a reply identifies phone firmware 9.3.2 as the suspected bug.
uncertainty: The firmware cause and remedy are participant-attributed and bound to an old release; no present-day product claim is implied. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.

claim: Specific error diagnosis and participant-reported configuration resolution. An inbound INVITE reached a CUCM node that was not in the trunk's device-pool call-manager group and received a 503. The thread explains that trunk ingress node membership and dial-peer node preference must align; changing preference resolved calls for the reporter. Outcome noted in the thread: The reporter states that reversing publisher/subscriber dial-peer preference made calls work; the discussion also points to all-node trunk operation in later versions.
versionOrJurisdiction: Historical Cisco VoIP mailing-list post dated 2013-04-10; product context: A reply notes that CUCM 8.x and later can accept a SIP trunk on all nodes; the exact customer's version is not identified.
uncertainty: This is a historical cluster/trunk routing example, not a claim that all 503 responses have this cause. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.

claim: Incident report plus unconfirmed troubleshooting hypotheses. After replacing an ISDN/H.323 gateway path with centralized SIP, a UCCX IVR call received a 404 despite a reported dial-peer match. A reply suggests CSS/partition visibility or SIP-trunk device-pool context as hypotheses. Outcome noted in the thread: No resolution is present in the sampled post; the proposed causes remain hypotheses.
versionOrJurisdiction: Historical Cisco VoIP mailing-list post dated 2019-10-13; product context: CUCM/UCCX/CUBE releases are not stated in the archived post.
uncertainty: The thread is incomplete and does not prove the suggested class-of-service or device-pool cause. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.
